issues.description: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS conflates literal delimiter characters with symbolic OpenAPI style names in a single namespace
issues.detail: The mapping mixes identity entries (',' -> ',', '|' -> '|', ' ' -> ' ') with OpenAPI aliases ('pipeDelimited' -> '|', 'spaceDelimited' -> ' '), serving simultaneously as an allowlist and a translation table. A cleaner decomposition is a small set/frozenset of accepted literal characters plus a tiny alias dict for the symbolic names. This would make extension obvious (e.g., future 'tabDelimited'), eliminate the redundant identity entries, and remove the risk of asymmetric updates between the character and the symbolic-name halves.

issues.description: Delimiter validation only fires inside the isinstance(items, str) branch, so the same bad argument raises or is silently accepted depending on request shape
issues.detail: Calling get_param_as_list('x', delimiter=';') raises ValueError when the value is a single string but silently accepts the bogus delimiter when the parameter appeared multiple times, was missing, or was already pre-split by auto_parse_qs_csv. Same call, same bad argument, different behavior depending on unrelated upstream state. Validate the delimiter argument once at the top of the function so the contract is consistent regardless of how (or whether) the value arrived.

issues.description: delimiter parameter contract is under-specified: typed as str | None but only five values accepted, and the new ValueError is undocumented
issues.detail: The signature declares delimiter: str | None, but the runtime accepts only five strings (',', '|', ' ', 'pipeDelimited', 'spaceDelimited') and raises ValueError on anything else. The Raises section of the docstring does not mention this new failure mode. Narrow the type to a Literal of the accepted values (or expose them as named constants/Enum) so static analysis can catch bad call sites, and document the new exception in the Raises block.

issues.description: Interaction with auto_parse_qs_csv and pre-split list values is encoded in tests but not stated as a postcondition in the docstring
issues.detail: When the value has already been turned into a list (multi-instance param or auto_parse_qs_csv), delimiter becomes a silent no-op. Two callers passing semantically identical HTTP inputs can get materially different results from the same call. The Note hints obliquely at this but never names auto_parse_qs_csv or specifies the postcondition. State the rule explicitly in the contract (Returns/Notes) so users learn it from the docstring rather than from reading the implementation or tests.

issues.description: Empty-string, blank-token, and trailing-delimiter edge cases are not covered by tests
issues.detail: The docstring promises that keep_blank_qs_values has no effect on the secondary delimiter split, but no test pins this behavior. Likewise there is no test for inputs like '', 'a,,b', 'a,b,' (trailing delimiter), or whitespace around tokens. For a feature whose entire job is splitting strings, these are exactly the regressions the next maintainer will want pinned. Add explicit assertions so the documented behavior is locked down.

issues.description: Interaction between delimiter and the transform callable is not tested
issues.detail: The function's invariant is that each returned element has been passed through transform. The new tests do not exercise the combination of delimiter and transform (e.g., get_param_as_list('xs', delimiter='|', transform=int)). Add a test that locks in this invariant so a future refactor of the split ordering cannot silently break it.

issues.description: Overload signatures use `= None` defaults where the rest of the file's overload stubs use `= ...`
issues.detail: All six @overload signatures declare `delimiter: str | None = None`, but the surrounding overloads consistently use `= ...` (Ellipsis) as the placeholder default (e.g., `store: StoreArg = ...`, `default: list[str] | None = ...`). Mixing literal `= None` into the overloads is stylistically inconsistent and may confuse static analyzers. Align with the file's convention by using `= ...` in the overloads and keeping `= None` only on the implementation.

issues.description: Error message leaks dict insertion order into a user-visible string
issues.detail: The ValueError reports tuple(_PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS), whose order is the dict's insertion order. This is observable, unspecified, and the kind of incidental property that becomes load-bearing the moment someone writes a test against the message text. Sort the keys or partition them into characters and symbolic names with a stable presentation so implementation order does not escape into the public contract.

issues.description: Raising bare ValueError from a request-parsing helper conflates programmer error with request error
issues.detail: get_param_as_list is documented to channel bad client input into HTTPBadRequest. A bad delimiter argument is a programmer error, not a request error, but it surfaces as a bare ValueError from inside a request handler — the kind of exception Falcon normally turns into a 500. Validate delimiter once at call time and consider a distinct exception type (or document the ValueError clearly) so the two failure modes stay separated.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-scoped feature whose implementation logic is sound, but whose API boundary and contract are under-specified. The dominant consensus concern (flagged by all six reviewers) is that _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS conflates literal delimiter characters with symbolic OpenAPI style names in a single namespace that doubles as an allowlist; a frozenset of accepted characters plus a small alias dict would be cleaner and safer to extend. The contract is leaky: delimiter is typed as str but only five values are accepted, the new ValueError is undocumented in Raises, validation only fires inside the isinstance(items, str) branch (so the same bad argument can raise or be silently accepted depending on request shape), and the no-op interaction with auto_parse_qs_csv and pre-split lists is encoded in tests rather than stated as a postcondition. Test coverage gaps include empty/blank/trailing-delimiter cases, transform interaction, and the keep_blank_qs_values claim. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on contract and validation hygiene; the underlying mechanism lands cleanly once those are addressed.
